pointers.sentence: Since 5.1 the methods of `RequestFactory`, `AsyncRequestFactory`, `Client` and `AsyncClient` take query_params, a mapping that becomes the query string of any method's request: `RequestFactory.generic` url-encodes it as the environ's `"QUERY_STRING"`, `AsyncRequestFactory.generic` as the scope's `"query_string"` (`django/test/client.py:RequestFactory.generic`, `django/test/client.py:AsyncRequestFactory.generic`).

Since 5.1 the methods of `RequestFactory`, `AsyncRequestFactory`, `Client` and `AsyncClient` take query_params, a mapping that becomes the query string of any method's request: `RequestFactory.generic` url-encodes it as the environ's `"QUERY_STRING"`, `AsyncRequestFactory.generic` as the scope's `"query_string"` (`django/test/client.py:RequestFactory.generic`, `django/test/client.py:AsyncRequestFactory.generic`).
On `RequestFactory.get` and `RequestFactory.head`, whose data is the query too, giving both is a `ValueError` (`django/test/client.py:RequestFactory.get`).

`ClientMixin` declares `ClientMixin.asession`, `ClientMixin.alogin`, `ClientMixin.aforce_login` and `ClientMixin.alogout` (5.0), coroutine twins of the session property and of the login and logout methods, on both clients (`django/test/client.py:ClientMixin.alogin`; [Sessions and logins in the test client: `ClientMixin.login` and `force_login`](../testing/client-login.md#the-asynchronous-methods)).

`AsyncClient`'s methods have taken `follow=True` since 5.0, but `ClientMixin._follow_redirect`, which it shares with `Client`, reads the request's WSGI keys for a relative Location and for a 307 or 308, and a scope has none: in a run, `AsyncClient` raised `KeyError` for both, which `Client` followed (`django/test/client.py:ClientMixin._follow_redirect`; [The test client: `Client` and `ClientHandler`](../testing/client.md#asyncclient-and-asyncclienthandler)).

`ClientMixin.force_login`, given no backend, takes the first entry of `AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS` whose class overrides `BaseBackend.get_user` or `BaseBackend.aget_user`, by which later requests find the user; before 6.2 a backend that answers only permissions could be chosen (`django/test/client.py:ClientMixin._get_backend`).

Since 5.2 `TransactionTestCase.setUpClass`, for a class that is not a `TestCase`, runs the first test's `_pre_setup`, a class method, and sets `SimpleTestCase._pre_setup_ran_eagerly` so that `SimpleTestCase._setup_and_call` does not run it again (`django/test/testcases.py:TransactionTestCase.setUpClass`).

Since 5.2 `django/test/testcases.py` sets `__unittest = True`, the mark by which `unittest` leaves a module's frames out of a reported traceback, so a failing assertion of Django's is reported at the test's own line and, the release notes add, `--pdb` enters the test method (`django/test/testcases.py:__unittest`; [One test, in order: `SimpleTestCase`](../testing/simple-test-case.md)).

Since 5.2 `django/test/testcases.py` sets `__unittest = True`, the mark by which `unittest` leaves a module's frames out of a reported traceback, so a failing assertion of Django's is reported at the test's own line and, the release notes add, `--pdb` enters the test method (`django/test/testcases.py:__unittest`; [One test, in order: `SimpleTestCase`](../testing/simple-test-case.md)).

Since 5.1, "to enforce test isolation" in the release notes' words, it also replaces `BaseDatabaseWrapper.ensure_connection` for the class, refusing a new connection to such an alias in any thread: in a run, a query in a thread the test started raised `DatabaseOperationForbidden` for "threaded connections" (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.ensure_connection_patch_method`; [Which databases a test uses: `databases`](../testing/test-databases.md)).
| `SimpleTestCase.assertContains`, `SimpleTestCase.assertNotContains` | the message ends with the body, as bytes | 5.1 | `django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.assertContains` |
| the same, on a streaming response | can be called again: the body read is put back as `StreamingHttpResponse.streaming_content` | 6.1 | `django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase._assert_contains` |
| `SimpleTestCase.assertInHTML` | the message ends with the haystack; `": "` follows a msg_prefix | 5.1 | `django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.assertInHTML` |
| `SimpleTestCase.assertNotInHTML` | new: `assertInHTML` with `count=0` | 5.1 | `django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.assertNotInHTML` |
| `SimpleTestCase.assertURLEqual` | `": "` follows a msg_prefix | 5.1 | `django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.assertURLEqual` |

| `SimpleTestCase.assertFormError`, `SimpleTestCase.assertFormSetError` | take a form or a formset, not a response and a name; `errors=None`, once no errors, is now `[None]` | 5.0 | `django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.assertFormError` |
| assertFormsetError | removed for `assertFormSetError` | 5.1 | `django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.assertFormSetError` |
| assertQuerysetEqual | removed for `TransactionTestCase.assertQuerySetEqual` | 5.1 | `django/test/testcases.py:TransactionTestCase.assertQuerySetEqual` |

`--durations` (5.0) is added by `DiscoverRunner.add_arguments` and passed to `unittest.TextTestRunner`, which reports the slowest tests (`django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner.get_test_runner_kwargs`; [The runner: the test command and `DiscoverRunner`](../testing/runner.md)).

Since 6.0 a parallel run works under the forkserver start method, which `_init_worker` treats as spawn: each worker starts without the parent's state, sets Django and the test environment up again and takes the parent's database settings (`django/test/runner.py:_init_worker`; [Running in parallel: `ParallelTestSuite`](../testing/parallel.md)).

Since 6.1 `setup_test_environment` gives each alias of a project's `MAILERS` the local-memory backend, and sets `EMAIL_BACKEND` only without it (`django/test/utils.py:setup_test_environment`; [What changed in mail and tasks](mail-and-tasks.md)).

The extra_tests argument of `DiscoverRunner.build_suite` and `DiscoverRunner.run_tests` went in 5.0, but both still take `**kwargs` and use none, so the argument is accepted and ignored (`django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner.build_suite`).

`setup_databases` serializes the rows a class with `serialized_rollback` gets back after every test database is made, which its comment says is for mirrors and routing, and, called by the runner, only for the aliases such classes use (`django/test/utils.py:setup_databases`; [Test databases: `BaseDatabaseCreation`](../backends/creation.md)).

The serialize argument of `BaseDatabaseCreation.create_test_db`, which when true serializes one database as it is made, warns with `RemovedInDjango2028Warning` whenever it is not None (6.0); the release notes name `BaseDatabaseCreation.serialize_db_to_string` in its place, the warning's message a DatabaseCreation.serialize_test_db that no class defines (`django/db/backends/base/creation.py:BaseDatabaseCreation.create_test_db`; [What still warns: the deprecations and the releases that end them](deprecations.md)).

The SERIALIZE test setting went in 5.0, deprecated in 4.0 as inferable from the tests' `serialized_rollback` (`docs/releases/4.0.txt`); nothing reads the key now (`django/db/utils.py:ConnectionHandler.configure_settings`).
